title: Elastic tier gating with budget-aware queue weights and regional fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Free, paid, and enterprise customers must be routed to capacity with predictable latency and cost while respecting per-tenant and per-plan token budgets. During regional capacity pressure we need deterministic behavior: preserve enterprise latency targets, degrade paid gracefully, and queue/drop free requests in a way that is transparent to customers. Existing admission controllers either hard-block (causing sharp outages) or apply simple FIFO quotas that cause latency cliffs and poor tail behavior.

Proposal: Implement an elastic tier-gating admission controller that assigns dynamic queue weights based on remaining budget (token credits), recent consumption velocity, and regional capacity signals. The controller will: 1) compute a per-tenant admission score combining tier priority (enterprise > paid > free), current budget fraction, and region health; 2) map scores to probabilistic admission rates and queue weights (soft-gating) rather than hard rejects where feasible; 3) support deterministic fallbacks to cheaper/quantized model variants in the same region or to a remote region when latency/throughput tradeoffs are acceptable; 4) expose configuration knobs for burst windows, emergency preemption, and fairness decay windows.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller returns an admission decision and a weight (0.0-1.0) within 1ms p50 on the fast path
Enterprise requests sustain <50ms median token latency under simulated region pressure while paid degrades smoothly and free is rate limited
Automated tests cover scoring logic, weight mapping, and fallback model selection
Console dashboard shows per-tier admission rate, budget burn, and regional spillover with historical trends
Configuration supports canary rollout and an emergency bypass flag for SRE intervention
implementation_notes: Add admission scoring module into the router pipeline immediately after auth: score = tier_weight * f(budget_fraction) * region_health_boost
budget_fraction calculation: remaining_tokens / monthly_commit_tokens, with an exponential smoothing over 5 minutes to avoid oscillation
Map score -> admission_weight using a configurable sigmoid with two parameters: slope and inflection. Default slope tuned to favor enterprise at low budget_fraction
When admission_weight < 0.2, route to fallback model variants in the same region (quantized or smaller) before considering cross-region spill
Introduce a 'soft-preempt' flag: temporarily reduce admission_weight for low-priority tenants during sustained SLO violations (>3m) rather than immediate reject
Add config objects to Console: per-tier default weights, emergency_preempt_ttl, cross_region_allowed(boolean), fallback_model_list ordering
PRs: backend admission controller (link placeholder) https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/621, runtime fallback adapter https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1743
E2E load test harness: extend existing traffic-sim to run mixed-tier workloads with synthetic regional outages and verify SLOs
Rollout plan: feature flag behind routing.elastic_tier_gating, canary to 10% of traffic on dedicated then 1 customer in hosted with opt-in
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Created ticket after on-call incident where free customers caused a cascading queue buildup in ap-southeast-1. Initial design sketched with Priya and Diego.
2025-02-15 Priya Patel (PM): Confirmed customer impact prioritization. Suggest adding an explicit 'min-guarantee' for enterprise to avoid cold-start tail regressions.

2025-02-18 Diego Alvarez (SRE): Performed preliminary capacity tests. Observed 40% tail latency increase when using hard rejects. Soft gating shows better tail behavior but needs careful smoothing to avoid oscillation.

2025-02-21 UX review (Ana Ribeiro): Console needs a clear visualization for 'spillover' and an explanation for why a request used a fallback model. Recommended an audit log entry for fallback decisions.

2025-02-25 Liam O'Connor: Implemented scoring skeleton and unit tests. Pushed initial PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/621. Benchmarks: scoring p50 0.6ms, p99 1.8ms on dev instance.

2025-02-27 Maya Chen: Security review requested. We should ensure fallback model choices don't violate data residency contracts for enterprise tenants. Marked security_review_required=true and added ENG-45800 for KMS/audit checks.
2025-02-28 SRE (Diego): Load test run 3/3 with mixed traffic. Enterprise SLO met, paid degrade path shows acceptable latency laddering; free flow reduced 72% of token burn during peak.
2025-03-01 PM (Priya): Approved canary plan. Next step: Console feature and telemetry onboarding. Assigning Console work to DES-231 for dashboard tiles.
notes_for_reviewers: Check fairness: ensure small enterprise tenants don't starve paid customers in a multi-tenant host when enterprise has burst credits
Review fallback model ordering: preference for same-region quantized variants before cross-region full models to minimize P99 increases
Validate emergency_preempt_ttl semantics—should be observable and reversible from the Console
Ensure telemetry tags include customer_tier and tenant_id hashed to a stable id for downstream billing correlation
